---
title: "Testing Mixed Effect in R vs Python"
output: html_notebook
---

 

```{R Load Data}
library('reticulate')
py_install("pandas")
pd <- import("pandas")

# Load the file using the pandas read_pickle method
summaryData <- pd$read_pickle('/users/frederictheunissen/Desktop/summary_stats.pkl')

summary(summaryData)
```

```{R Select Data}
information_threshold = 6.0 # in bits/s
snr_threshold = 0.0 # unitless
rate_threshold = 1.0 # average evoked rate in spikes/s
data_size_threshold = 2000 # Requiring at leat 2000 spikes.

summaryData$Auditory <- (summaryData$snr > snr_threshold) & (summaryData$cumInfo > information_threshold) & (summaryData$rate > rate_threshold) & (summaryData$rate*summaryData$data_length/1000 > data_size_threshold)

r2_threshold = 0.2
summaryData$Modeled = ( (summaryData$r2segId/summaryData$r2Ceil) > r2_threshold) & summaryData$Auditory

``` 

``` {R Mixed Effect}
library(lme4)

full_model <- lmer('(r2Seg/r2segId) ~ unit_type*brain_area + (1|bird)', data = summaryData, subset = summaryData$Modeled, REML = FALSE)
null_model <- lmer('(r2Seg/r2segId) ~ unit_type + (1|bird)', data = summaryData, subset = summaryData$Modeled, REML = FALSE)

summary(full_model)
summary(null_model)

anova(full_model, null_model)
```
